newsitem.title: USA: New York utilities Brooklyn Union, Lilco to merge.
newsitem.headline: New York utilities Brooklyn Union, Lilco to merge.

text.p: Brooklyn Union Gas Co. and the Long Island Lighting Co. (Lilco) said Sunday they agreed to merge in a stock deal that would create a $4 billion electric and gas company.
The deal comes after years of political wrangling over Lilco and its Shoreham nuclear power plant -- which never opened -- and state proposals to take over the utility.

The deal was called key to lowering electric rates on New York's Long Island, which has some of the highest rates in the nation, due mostly to Lilco's multibillion-dollar debt for the Shoreham nuclear plant.

"The consolidation of our neighbouring companies will result in synergy savings in excesss of $1 billion over 10 years, which will provide rate reductions to customers," Lilco Chairman William Catacosinos said in a statement.
Lilco won a round recently, when a state judge on Nov. 7 ordered local county and city governments to repay the company as much as $1.1 billion in taxes for the Shoreham plant.

The companies said they will continue discussions with the Long Island Power Authority over the agency's proposal to acquire the Shoreham plant along with its debt, which would be refinanced, in a bid to reduce rates for local customers.

Regulators also have been anxious to introduce competition into the area, and have considered proposals to import power across Long Island Sound, which separates Long Island from Connecticut, from New England or Canada.

"We greet the announcement ... as a positive development which will help us to complete negotiations on a plan to reduce utility rates and introduce long-term competition on Long Island," Long Island Power Authority Chairman Frank Zarb said in a statement.

Brooklyn Union provides natural gas service to the New York City boroughs of Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island. The company is regarded as an innovative utility known for its customer service and savvy management.
Hicksville, N.Y.-based Lilco provides power and gas to the eastern Long Island counties of Nassau and Suffolk as well as parts of Queens.
The two companies serve a total of 2.2 million customers.

Under the merger, Brooklyn Union shareholders would get one share of the company to be formed from the merger for each share they now hold, and Lilco shareholders would receive 0.803 shares of the new company.
Lilco shareholders would own about 66 percent of the new company, and Brooklyn Union shareholders would own about 34 percent. The deal was structured as a pooling of interest.
The combined value of the two companies at Friday's stock prices is $4 billion. Their annual revenues are about $4.5 billion, the companies said.
The companies said that after the merger Catacosinos, who is chairman and chief executive officer of Lilco, will be chairman and chief executive of the new company.

Robert Catell, chairman and chief executive of Brooklyn Union, will be president and chief operating officer. One year after closing, Catell will succeed Catacosinos as CEO, with Catacosinos continuing as chairman.
For Brooklyn Union, the merger offers access to a big new market where natural gas now plays a minor role.

"Our combination with Lilco opens up the substantial Long Island market for Brooklyn Union," Catell said in a statement. "This market is particularly attractive because there is a low penetration of gas as a percent of the total energy provision in that region."
